query: For boride-based components used in hot-dip aluminum-plating equipment, what single intervention could improve resistance to molten-aluminum corrosion? Formulate one hypothesis that identifies the intervention, explains its mechanism, predicts the improvement relative to an appropriate baseline, defines the conditions under which it should remain effective, cites supporting prior evidence, and specifies a controlled experiment whose results could falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: Applying a powder-pack boriding surface treatment to boride-based components will improve their resistance to molten-aluminum corrosion compared to untreated components.
generation.material_initial_state: Boride-based components as used in hot-dip aluminum-plating equipment without any specialized surface modification for high-temperature corrosion resistance.
generation.intervention: A powder-pack boriding surface treatment process applied to the components prior to their exposure to molten aluminum.
generation.conditions: Components are exposed to molten aluminum at typical plating temperatures; the treatment is expected to remain effective under these high-temperature, chemically aggressive molten-metal conditions.
generation.structural_mediator: The formation of a uniform, adherent boride-rich surface layer that serves as a corrosion barrier.
generation.mechanism: The boriding treatment creates a dense boride layer that impedes the diffusion of aluminum and oxygen, reducing the chemical reaction between the molten aluminum and the base material. This protective scale offers enhanced resistance to the corrosive attack of the molten aluminum by limiting its penetration and resulting degradation.
generation.predicted_outcome: Components receiving the powder-pack boriding treatment will show a measurable improvement in corrosion resistance (e.g., reduced weight loss and slower corrosion depth progression) relative to untreated components when immersed in molten aluminum.
generation.baseline: Untreated boride-based components typically used in hot-dip aluminum-plating equipment.
generation.boundary: The predicted improvement is expected under standard molten-aluminum exposure conditions (typical operating temperatures and exposure durations); performance under extreme or cyclic thermal conditions remains to be verified.
generation.uncertainty: The precise magnitude of corrosion resistance improvement and the long-term durability of the boride layer under repeated thermal cycles require further experimental validation.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare two groups of identical boride-based component samples. Subject one group to the powder-pack boriding treatment while leaving the other group untreated. Expose both groups to molten aluminum at standard plating temperatures for a fixed duration in a controlled environment.
measurements: Corrosion depth analysis using cross-sectional microscopy (e.g., SEM)
Surface phase analysis (e.g., XRD) to confirm the presence and integrity of the boride layer
Hardness testing of the surface layer
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the treated samples do not exhibit a statistically significant improvement (e.g., a meaningful reduction in weight loss and corrosion depth compared to the untreated controls) under the defined experimental parameters, the hypothesis will be considered falsified.

chosen.approach: Powder-pack boriding surface treatment for HEA components
